name: Attention sentences + portrait figure
reason: The calmest home possible. Ranked sentences carry the decisions, inline actions sit inside each sentence, and the portrait map is a figure that confirms geography without competing.

name: Latitude metro + attention rail
reason: The Round 4 signature survives inside a product. The floating rail stays out of the way, and the attention rail narrows or moves under the metro at 1199. Distinctive and legible.

name: Ledger + portrait map + action strip
reason: The most implementable and scalable, and the closest to a classic tool. The micro-journey rows keep it FleetOS, but the three-column skeleton is generic and the map column is half wallpaper.

name: Drivers as day ribbons (edge nav)
reason: Every driver on one clock with legal state in the row, and a sentence header. Edge navigation reads as a ruler and disappears into the margin. Dense and calm, it scales to 40.

name: Fleet rows with load silhouettes
reason: Silhouettes show load and state at a glance, with location and next maintenance in each row. Good, but repeated silhouettes become texture past 15 rows. Needs a compact glyph mode.

name: Portrait country, exceptions bound by leaders
reason: ISA-101 geography: grey routes, ink only on exceptions, with labels flowing to a right gutter by leader lines. No panel and no landscape waste.

name: Forbidden regions plane + rule column
reason: All restrictions as space-time barriers with every transport as a string, plus a left column that names each rule and its exposure. The operation-wide restriction view.

name: Number + road + gauges
reason: The Round 4 signature in a real shell. The number anchors, the road carries time and place, and the gauges sit in the footer zone. Reflows from a stacked 1199 to a 1920 with week context.

name: Ribbon instrument + legal bands + bottom stops
reason: Clear and implementable: chip anchor, ruler lenses, ribbon with legal bands and an attached action at the pause. But it's the Round 1 D-01 page with a rail, missing the road's distinctiveness.

name: Identity column + time spine with lens rows
reason: Lenses are rows added to one shared clock (activity, legality, stops, documents, vehicle), so adding context never creates a new page. The identity column stays fixed. The most dynamic-friendly grammar.

name: Legal reach cone as the instrument
reason: The cone holds the full legal answer, and the chip anchor plus ruler lenses keep identity without stealing scale. Edge actions stay out of the instrument. It needs a one-time explanation.

name: Person ⇄ machine joints on the drawing
reason: Compatibility joints between the person card and the drawing work. The receding crumb is elegant, but the joints still read as a diagram (Round 1's D-04 problem) once surrounded by UI.

name: Legal corridor on real geography + day crossing
reason: Round 3's best Driver spatial state inside the shell. The floating rail recedes, the day ribbon crosses the map as a band, and the confirm action is attached to Santarém on the map.

name: Sentence + rule path + exposure plane
reason: Honest and readable: the sentence, the conditions path and the driver's crossing on a small plane. But the driver anchor feels incidental; this belongs to the restriction anchor.

name: Commitments + instrument + map + papers
reason: Everything at once works for a power user at 1920. At 1440 the four regions compete and the road loses its scale. Density is achieved, distinctiveness drops.

name: Elevation + plan hero, unload order, docked inset
reason: The machine is the page. The elevation and plan are aligned, the unload order is drawn to the doors, and the action sits at the doors. A tiny docked inset says where without a map region.

name: Drawing sheet as the full page
reason: The drawing sheet is FleetOS's most distinctive vehicle state and reads as a complete product state. Lower dynamic potential: it's a document, not a workspace.

name: Component lifelines hung from the drawing
reason: Wear aligned to component position is right, but labels fight the drawing at 1440. It works at 1920 or with the sheet format.

name: Front silhouette vs gates + detail cutout
reason: The physical answer is centred, the gate outlines overlay the silhouette, and a circular street cutout says where the tightest gate is. Instantly understood.

name: Object docked to its marker on a dark corridor
reason: Beautiful, and the docked drawing keeps continuity. But dark tone for a daytime question breaks the 'grey is normal' language, so it's better as the paper variant.

name: Front page of the transport
reason: In a real shell the front page reads like a briefing, ideal for handover or client view. It's static, though: once things move, an editorial layout ages in minutes.

name: Decision fork + ISA-101 margin
reason: The Round 4 signature in a shell: a rail, a grey-normal margin and the fork on time. The 'execution' state has one obvious next action, attached to the recommended branch. Best execution layout.

name: People · equipment · places bands
reason: Bands show who and what is bound to each leg and make hand-overs visible. A good team view for multi-leg work, too heavy for single-driver transports.

name: Paper timeline over the open sheet
reason: Receipts on the top timeline, stamps above it, and the selected sheet at reading scale below. The documents of a transport finally read as evidence of events. Survives inside the shell.

name: Plan lineage + reissue proposal bar
reason: The proposal bar works here: revisions stack as plans, the pending change appears as rev. 8 drawn dashed, and the dark bar states the consequence. The clearest editing state in the set.

name: Strip + string chart + map + papers + strip actions
reason: It holds everything a power user wants, but at 1440 the string chart is cramped and the map column is decorative. Better as a 1920-only mode.

name: String chart + vertical corridor
map: vertical corridor on the chart's axis
reason: The strongest route state in context. The corridor column and the chart share the km axis, and the alternative's action sits on its dashed line. Reflows: at 1199 the corridor narrows to a ribbon; at 1920 a stop column appears.

name: Unrolled corridor + km strata
reason: The geology-section route as a full product state: the corridor band on top and strata for road, legality, fuel, restrictions and cargo. Edge nav and one attached action. Calm, dense, distinctive.

name: Full route + bottom strip bound by leaders
reason: Round 3's A3 archetype holds up in the shell: floating rail, edge actions and a distance-true strip bound to the geography. The most implementable spatial state.

name: Two strings + delta ledger + proposal
reason: Comparison as geometry: current and alternative strings on one chart, a delta ledger beside it, and the proposal bar for 'adopt alternative'. Clear recommendation and consequence.

name: Street approach + minute ticks + local strip
reason: Street-level OSM, the final approach with minute ticks, the underpass marked in place, and a strip re-scoped to the last 36 km. The local stop state the product never had.

name: Sheet centre stage + margin notes + tape
reason: A strong reading experience, but the dossier is really W-24 with the timeline compressed. Two document layouts are one too many.

name: Two sheets, marks on the fields, cause in the margin
reason: The sheets themselves are the interface: diff marks on the fields and the cause written in the margin. The receding crumb gives the whole width to paper.

name: Cause → sheet → consequence + proposal
reason: Reissue reads left to right (change, affected field, consequences) and the proposal bar makes it a single, explicit commitment. The editing grammar for every document.

name: Verdict sentence + conditions path + evidence fold
reason: Very clear and cheap to build, but it is a sentence and a row of boxes. It needs the two-futures or plane to earn its screen.

name: Axle gap hero + two futures
reason: The missing fact is drawn where it lives (the axle), with the world split on it and priced. The task is attached to the drawing. Distinctive and actionable.

name: Barrier on the plane + affected rows
reason: Solid, but a single-restriction variant of W-07. Keep W-07 and filter it by restriction instead of a separate layout.

name: Street segment + detail-A cutout + logic chip
reason: Round 3's G-09 holds in the shell: the ring at street level, the physical section in a CAD bubble, and the logic as a small chip. No panel, all bound to the place.
